caption: The drawing shows two detailed, technical views of a chair, rendered in black ink on a yellowed paper background. The left side of the drawing displays a front elevation of the chair, focusing on ornate, classical decorative elements incorporated into the chair’s backrest, including symmetrical columns, draped garlands, and a central urn motif, all bounded within a square outer frame. Detailed measurements are provided for each decorative part and overall chair dimensions, with the entire height specified as 36 3/4 inches, a seat width of 21 inches, and a leg height of 17 3/4 inches. The right side presents a rear view of the chair, outlining the shape and dimensions of the seat frame, which curves along the back, as well as the legs and seat construction. Measurements are annotated throughout the drawing for clarity, indicating thickness, width, and placement of structural components. At the bottom right corner, a title block records the drawing scale as 3/8 inch to 1 inch, the date as June 1936, the creator as Michael Terkur, and the address and institution as the Metropolitan Museum of Art in New York City. The composition is technical, with all lines and text in consistent black ink, and the paper has slightly aged with areas of light staining, especially near the corners.
title: Side Chair
